author: Michael McLaughlin
title: Early voting begins: what's on the ballot? - NewsBreak
text:
By Michael McLaughlin ,
1 hours ago Early and absentee voting began Wednesday, Oct. 15, for a special election ahead of November 4, where voters in ten counties will decide on various issues.
One issue that has been watched closely is a proposal in Greene County that places a 3% tax on visitors staying in hotels or motels, which would be used to finance the construction of a new convention center in Springfield. The Springfield City Council has already approved the measure, and it is now up to voters to make the final decision at the ballot box.
“The new convention center could bring more visitors and money into the city,” said Amanda Ohlensehlen, Economic Vitality Director for the City of Springfield. “It would help attract major events, new sporting activities, and support local programs and initiatives.”
The increase to the hotel/motel license tax would be a component of an overall incentive package.
The issues that voters will be asked to approve in other counties are listed below:
Barry County Cassville Fire Protection District tax question Shall the district be authorized to impose a ½-cent sales tax to fund the district, tied to a reduction in the property tax levy equal to half of the funds raised by this tax if approved?
Benton County Morgan County R-1 School District tax question Shall the district increase for 20 years the operating tax levy by 63 cents per $100 of assessed valuation to construct and improve facilities, including a new athletic complex? Levy would stand at $3.95 per $100 if approved by voters.
State Fair Community College tax question Shall the college be authorized to increase the operating tax levy by 10 cents per $100 of assessed valuation, placing the levy at 50 cents per $100?
Hermitage/Wheatland School District merger and tax question Shall the Wheatland and Hermitage school districts form a new district with a property tax rate of $2.48 per $100 is assessed valuation? (Also on some Hickory County ballots)
Camden County Mack’s Creek School District bond issue Shall the district be authorized to issue $1.5 million in general obligation bonds for improvement, repair, and renovation of facilities, including kitchen, cafeteria, gymnasium and weight room? (No increase in debt service levy)
Christian County ¼-cent property tax hike for Nixa Fire Protection District Shall the Board of Directors of the Nixa Fire Protection District levy an additional tax of not more than twenty-five cents per $100 of assessed valuation? (Also on some Stone County ballots)
County-wide use tax Shall the county impose a local use tax on goods purchased from out of state at the same rate as the local sales tax rate?
Hickory County Hermitage/Wheatland School District merger and tax question Shall the Wheatland and Hermitage school districts form a new district with a property tax rate of $2.48 per $100 is assessed valuation? (Also on some Benton County ballots)
Polk County City of Bolivar contract for electric utility Shall the city of Bolivar contract with Southwest Electric Cooperative for non-exclusive rights to provide electricity to the city for 20 years, as provided in city Ordinance No. 4071?
St. Clair County Osceola ½-cent public safety sales tax Shall the city of Osceola impose a ½-cent sales tax for the purpose of improving public safety?
Stone County ¼-cent property tax hike for Nixa Fire Protection District Shall the Board of Directors of the Nixa Fire Protection District levy an additional tax of not more than twenty-five cents per $100 of assessed valuation? (Also on some Christian County ballots)
Texas County Homestead tax relief Shall the county exempt citizens from increases in the property tax on residences?
Road and bridge question Shall the county replace the expiring ½-cent capital improvement sales tax with a ½-cent retail sales tax, including utilities, for the maintenance of roads, culverts and bridges?
The deadline to register for the Nov. 4 elections is Oct. 8 for anyone not currently registered in his or her county.
